title: KEEL token emissions are permanently disabled beyond Genesis Supply, but Sky Governance keeps a Risk-Capital-triggered override
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.1.4.2.1.1.6 states that "token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are permanently disabled; this cannot be reverted by Keel Governance," then immediately carves out that "Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Keel is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework."

The asymmetry is the whole design. Dilution is removed from the hands of the party that benefits from it — Keel and its tokenholders — and left only with the party that would be *harmed* by Keel's insolvency. This makes the supply cap credible in exactly the way a self-imposed cap is not: the actor who could break it has no incentive to, and the actor with the incentive to break it cannot.

The trigger is narrow and adverse: not "whenever Sky Governance prefers," but specifically a Risk Capital violation where the Risk Framework requires emissions (see A.3.2 - Risk Capital). Newly issued KEEL therefore functions as a recapitalization instrument of last resort — the tokenholders absorb dilution precisely at the moment Keel has failed to hold sufficient risk capital.

Read as a promise to holders, "permanently disabled" is conditional rather than absolute. That is not a loophole so much as an honest statement of seniority: Sky's solvency ranks above KEEL's supply guarantee.
description: Keel Governance cannot re-enable emissions at all; Sky Governance can, but only where Keel violates Risk Capital requirements and the Risk Framework requires new issuance.
